title: Ukraine's commander-in-chief Zaluzhnyi describes a stalemate in The Economist
body:
On 1-2 November 2023 The Economist published an interview with and essay by General Valerii Zaluzhnyi, Commander-in-Chief of Ukraine's Armed Forces. Zaluzhnyi said the front had reached a stalemate. He argued that neither side could advance because both were closely matched technologically, and he compared the situation to the First World War.

On 4 November 2023, at a press conference with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected the idea that the front was deadlocked. He said Russia controlled the airspace and that Ukraine needed more air defence to advance, linking this to the completion of F-16 pilot training. He recalled that similar stalemate claims had been made in 2022 before the liberation of parts of Kharkiv Oblast. Zelensky rejected talks or concessions with Russia and warned against a frozen conflict, which he said would mean giving up a third of the country. He denied that Western leaders were pressuring him to negotiate.

Other reactions followed. White House National Security Council coordinator John Kirby said the essay supported the urgent need for more aid to Ukraine. The Kremlin said there was no stalemate and that Russia was continuing its war. Ihor Zhovkva, deputy head of the Office of the President, said the military should not discuss front-line developments publicly. NBC News reported that US and EU officials had begun discussing with Ukraine the possibility of peace talks with Russia.
